UPSTREAM: arch/x86: Fix car_active for CONFIG_NO_CAR_GLOBAL_MIGRATION Change 76ab2b7 ("arch/x86: allow global .bss objects without CAR_GLOBAL") allowed use of global .bss objects and hence moved around the macros resulting in car_active returning 0 even for those boards where CAR is actually active but do not require global migration. This resulted in boards getting stuck when doing a reset in verstage because the code flow incorrectly assumed that there was no CAR active and hence triggered a cache invalidate. This change fixes the above issue by returning 1 for car_active if ENV_CACHE_AS_RAM is set even if global migration is not required. BUG=b:109717603 TEST=Verified that board reset does not trigger cache invalidate in verstage and does not result in board hang. Change-Id: Ib13b82585f7291fb89cd03f61a30d7ca75b1c0e3 Signed-off-by: Furquan Shaikh <furquan@google.com> Original-Commit-Id: 890788eb6304a7b88906422a97dbb5c1bc717ee4 Original-Change-Id: I182f3e4277c57d6c50f7fcac2be72514896b3c61 Original-Signed-off-by: Furquan Shaikh <furquan@google.com> Original-Reviewed-on: https://review.coreboot.org/29555 Original-Tested-by: build bot (Jenkins) <no-reply@coreboot.org> Original-Reviewed-by: Peichao Li <peichao.wang@bitland.corp-partner.google.com> Original-Reviewed-by: Nick Chen <nickchen@ami.corp-partner.google.com> Original-Reviewed-by: Aaron Durbin <adurbin@chromium.org> Original-Reviewed-by: Justin TerAvest <teravest@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1329754 Commit-Ready: Furquan Shaikh <furquan@chromium.org> Tested-by: Furquan Shaikh <furquan@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Furquan Shaikh <furquan@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Justin TerAvest <teravest@chromium.org>

power: Prioritize Mode::CLOSED over Mode::TABLET tablet_mode is based on lid angle or a physical switch like the one provided by Pixel Slate's detachable keyboard (provided through the EC). However, if we are in tablet mode, and the lid is closed, we should prioritize Mode::CLOSED over Mode::TABLET. This is especially important for management of external wakeup sources, such as the Brydge G-Type which connects to the system via Bluetooth, does not trigger the EC's "tablet/clamshell" switch, but can trigger the lid switch via magnets. Without this patch, the bluetooth module's wakeup is configured on and we're running into spurious wakeups while lid closed from the Brydge keyboard. Signed-off-by: Benson Leung <bleung@chromium.org> BUG=b:119287727 TEST=pair Brydge G-Type keyboard, enter Guest mode. watch -n 0.1 cat /sys/bus/usb/devices/1-3/power/wakeup Close the lid. Check that before suspending, the wakeup property goes to disabled. Check that system stays asleep, no spurious wakeups due to the keyboard or trackpad. FEATURES="test" emerge-nocturne power_manager Check that HandleTabletMode test passes. UPSTREAM: ec/google/chromeec: Configure EC_SYNC_IRQ as level triggered EC_SYNC_IRQ from EC to host is level-triggered in practice and configuring it as edge-triggered on the host results in host missing events if there are multiple events queued on the EC side. This is because Linux kernel driver reads one event per irq and the EC does not de-assert the interrupt line until all events are drained out. This results in event queue being filled up completely on the EC and the host failing to see any of those events. This change configures EC_SYNC_IRQ as level triggered to allow the host to read events from the the EC as long as the line is asserted. BUG=b:118949877 Change-Id: Icbfdc3794699b358af57e1211f9b02a5485e2b46 Signed-off-by: Furquan Shaikh <furquan@google.com> Original-Commit-Id: 0d6349ee0d95a41aaa06ae89a87cb22e51075b01 Original-Change-Id: Id3fcfa0445f83865d57975a7bbc179dca047ba4c Original-Signed-off-by: Furquan Shaikh <furquan@google.com> Original-Reviewed-on: https://review.coreboot.org/29575 Original-Tested-by: build bot (Jenkins) <no-reply@coreboot.org> Original-Reviewed-by: Duncan Laurie <dlaurie@chromium.org> Original-Reviewed-by: Aseda Aboagye <aaboagye@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1330312 Commit-Ready: Furquan Shaikh <furquan@chromium.org> Tested-by: Furquan Shaikh <furquan@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Furquan Shaikh <furquan@chromium.org>

runner: Unify the code paths for report/non-report mode. We used to have slightly different logics in runTestsAndReport (report-mode; used when the test runner is run by "tast" command) and runTestsAndLog (non-report mode; used when the test runner is run directly). This change unifies the two funcs by making runTestsAndLog to call runTestsAndReport and convert its control message output to textual logs. Fortunately runTestsAndReport already parses control messages from bundles, so the only new message type to process is RunError, which now contains the exit status code to return. Several functions are updated to return *StatusError instead of error to make it statically safe to extract an exit code.
